title: Evaluating Multimodal LLMs across Text and Audio Modalities for Accessible Disaster Assistance
abstract: arXiv:2608.14651v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Effective disaster risk communication is a foundational humanitarian challenge, yet current emergency infrastructure fails to meet the needs of individuals with access and functional needs, including hard-of-hearing individuals, pregnant women, mothers with toddlers, and elderly individuals with dementia. Recent advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI), especially Multi-Modal Large Language Models (MM-LLMs), demonstrate powerful capabilities to serve diverse users across text, audio, image, and video modalities within a single unified system, such as a chatbot. translated_title: 评估多模态大语言模型在文本与音频模态下对无障碍灾害援助的支持能力
translated_abstract: 有效的灾害风险沟通是一项基础性的人道主义挑战，然而当前的应急基础设施无法满足具有行动和功能需求人群的需求，包括听力障碍者、孕妇、带幼儿的母亲以及患有痴呆症的老年人。人工智能（AI）的最新进展，特别是多模态大语言模型（MM-LLMs），展示了在单一统一系统（如聊天机器人）中通过文本、音频、图像和视频模态服务多样化用户的强大能力。然而，它们是否适合部署取决于一个很少受到审视的特性，即无论用户通过何种模态进行交流，这些系统是否都能产生一致且可操作的输出。在本文中，我们使用真实的紧急警报场景，对四种不同的模态进行了全面分析，以了解开放权重MM-LLMs的现状。
tldr: 本文通过真实紧急警报场景测试了开放权重多模态大语言模型在文本和音频模态下输出的一致性与可操作性，发现其跨模态表现存在差异，凸显了在无障碍灾害援助中需进一步优化模型以保障用户安全。
en_tdlr: This paper evaluates open-weight multimodal LLMs across text and audio modalities using real emergency alert scenarios, revealing inconsistencies in output that underscore the need for improved cross-modal reliability in accessible disaster assistance.
